Because each sandbox holds a real checkout, agents search it with grep and standard file tools instead of relying on broad semantic searches.

On an internal benchmark of 150 financial-document questions, this reached 0.627 answer accuracy versus about 0.37 for semantic search. https://t.co/w1nmA0N8yz

A single long-lived sandbox per project would need provisioning for peak load and months of uptime.

Instead, repositories live on S3-backed storage and each agent runs in its own ephemeral sandbox, so a crash loses only unsubmitted work. https://t.co/dglC3ZI6AX

The CLI holds a short-lived lock to serialize submits, and the Git service accepts a submit only if it builds on the head, the latest accepted commit.

Otherwise, the agent replays its change on the new head and resubmits. https://t.co/urIrVVwPL7

Git provides atomic multi-file commits, authorship, and queryable history.

A forge hosts the repository, controls who can update it, and adds PR review. Projects keep the first two and replace review with a check of each submit against a repository contract.

Agents collaborating on a long-running project face the same problem as engineers sharing a codebase.

Work must outlive ephemeral sandboxes, concurrent writes must not overwrite each other, and history must show who changed what.

This is how we built the filesystem behind Perplexity Projects as a Git forge for agents.

Each agent works in its own sandbox and commits to a shared repository where people and other agents can build on its work across sessions.

Both models are on Hugging Face: https://t.co/JHy1DhFaCT
On MADQA, 500 questions over 800 PDFs, it reaches 92.4%, the top result among retrievers. https://t.co/uxW8LDau2c

In agentic search, a GPT-OSS-120B agent using the 9B model answers 64.0% of BrowseComp+ questions correctly, 4.9 points ahead of the next ColBERT model, with fewer searches than any baseline. https://t.co/hFngH5ES7D

On Q2D-Web, about 70,000 production-derived search queries over 190M web documents, the 9B and 0.6B models reach 74.8% and 73.6% Recall@1000, against 69.3% for nemotron-embed-8b. https://t.co/FwltQP6jGN

Both sizes are distilled token by token from one 18B teacher, so they share one embedding space.

A corpus indexed with the 9B model can be searched with 0.6B queries. That lifts ViDoRe v3 from 62.3% to 63.5% with no added query cost. https://t.co/SglIFldtGQ
The models also embed images and rendered pages directly, so PDFs, slides, and scans are searched without OCR, keeping tables, figures, and layout that text extraction drops. https://t.co/iZmlOKG1ye

Dense embedding models compress each document into one vector, which loses detail as pages get longer or more visual.

pplx-embed-v2-late keeps a 128-dimensional vector per token and scores with MaxSim, so each query token is matched to its closest token in the document. https://t.co/vlax3OLOXF

We're releasing pplx-embed-v2-late, two late-interaction embedding models that retrieve text, images, and pages with a shared embedding space for cross-model querying.

Both models achieve frontier performance and are publicly available on Hugging Face.

https://t.co/AM7YEyQkKE https://t.co/fR8kaYmHs1

context-bench is a benchmark for context-aware retrieval, created and privately held by @turbopuffer. Its queries, documents and capabilities are inspired by conversations with turbopuffer customers.

It has 2,099 queries and 38,894 documents. We submitted for blind evaluation. https://t.co/IsHUVOl4gh

We overcome gold-chunk supervision limits by distilling relevance from our query-aware context compression model.

It scores every document token against the query. Aggregated into chunk-level targets, those scores train the embedder to retrieve answer and supporting chunks. https://t.co/PvP2TLX5Y9

Retrieval systems often split long documents into chunks, but this strips away the surrounding context.

Contextual embedding models fix this by encoding the whole document once and pooling chunk vectors afterward.

They are usually trained on one gold chunk per query.

We built a new way to train contextual embedding models, which encode each chunk of a document with the whole document in view.

pplx-embed-v2-context-9b-preview sets a new state of the art on ConTEB and @turbopuffer's new, privately held context-bench.
